quotes.text: Low code isn't less engineering. It's engineering without the cultural friction that normally forces someone to ask hard questions early.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concisely reframes low code as engineering that still needs design discipline.

quotes.text: Power platform does not enforce your intent. It enforces your configuration. If you didn't encode the boundary, the boundary does not exist.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures why governance has to be expressed as configuration, not intention.

quotes.text: Shadow IT mostly stores data in the wrong place. Annoying, risky, usually recoverable. Shadow automation executes. It moves data between systems.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A sharp distinction between shadow IT and the more dangerous shadow automation.

quotes.text: The critical rule is simple. Decisions can be uncertain. Execution cannot. Execution is the side effect layer.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core design rule of separating probabilistic decisions from deterministic execution.

quotes.text: So the rule is blunt. If you can't prove an action is safe to retry, you're not retrying. You're doubling down.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable warning against using retries without idempotency.

chapters.title: Power Automate is not a workflow tool
What the automation control plane really is
Anti-patterns: Christmas tree flows, API exhaustion, shadow automation
Direct path, design discipline and transaction-driven design
Child flows, early termination, expressions and flat nesting
KPIs, reference architecture and case study

takeaways: Power Automate should be governed as an automation control plane, because the platform enforces configuration, not intent.
Separate probabilistic decisions from deterministic execution: keep orchestration thin and put every side effect into idempotent child flows with receipts and bounded retries.
Measure explainability and ownership, such as mean time to explain, ownership coverage and API budget adherence, instead of counting flows and runs.
hook: Most organizations treat Power Automate as a simple workflow tool until outages, audit questions and runaway API costs prove otherwise. This episode is for architects, platform teams and IT leaders who run automation at enterprise scale. It gives you a control plane mental model and concrete patterns, from direct path flows and child flows as execution units to KPIs that make automation explainable.
